content: 1. Before initiating therapy in females of reproductive potential, it is essential to verify their pregnancy status. 2. Females of reproductive potential should be advised to use effective contraception during treatment and for a period of five months after the last dose. 3. Vomiting and/or diarrhea that occurs during therapy may interfere with the absorption of oral contraceptives, potentially reducing their effectiveness. 4. If vomiting and/or diarrhea occur during therapy, females should be instructed to use an additional non-oral method of effective contraception. 5. There is no available data regarding the presence of miltefosine in human or animal breast milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production. Due to the potential for serious adverse reactions, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment and for five months after the last dose. 6. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk, making the treatment generally acceptable. 7. Only 2% of the administered dose is absorbed. 8. To minimize gastrointestinal adverse effects, the medication should be taken with meals. 9. Capsules must be swallowed whole and should not be chewed or broken apart. 10. Patients should be instructed to complete the full course of therapy as prescribed. 11. Adding plans allows for the comparison of formulary status with other drugs in the same class. 12.
